While the audience enjoyed the performance, many struggled to distinguish the different sounds produced. Later, one of the recruits collapsed from fatigue and was rushed to the hospital. Dr. Kirabo, the army doctor, examined the patientbut had difficulty reading the patient's previous medical records. She suspected that the power of her spectacle lenses might have weakened. She also recommended a laser-based endoscopic procedure for a more detailed internal examination. Due to her tight schedule, Dr. Kirabo asked her assistant to help verify the power of her lenses. The assistant placed the medical records 20 cm in front of the lens and observed that a real image was formed 60 cm on the oppositeside of the lens. They needed to determine whether the lens power was still within the acceptable range of +5.0 D to +6.0 D. Refractiveindex of the glass maierial is 1.47. Height of the medical records is 2em.

questions.text: During a space science lesson, students learned that scientists have recently discovered a planet beyond Earth that might be capable of supporting life. This sparked their curiosity, and they became eager to learn more. As they conducted further research using textbooks and the internet, they came across fascinating images, including: Photos of stars showing different colours and brightness. Satellite images showing wèather patterns and atmospheric colours over specific regions of the Earth. These discoveries led to a lively discussion. Some students believed that all the images were taken by the Hubble Space Telescope, while others argued that they were captured by the International Space Station (1SS). Confused and unable to agree, they approached you as a physics student to clarify for them the following activity;

subTasks.label: a
subTasks.text: Explaining the differences in the functions and uses of the Hubble Space Telescope and the International Space Station	(ISS).

subTasks.label: b
subTasks.text: Why stars appear in different colours and brightness and explain the significanceof this information and explanation of the key features of a planet that would make it capable of supporting life.

subTasks.label: c
subTasks.text: Identification and explanation of the key features of a planet that would make it capable of the supporting life.

subTasks.label: d
subTasks.text: A weather satellite	is programmed to transmit images back to Earth only under safe and useful conditions. For transmission to occur, the following logic must be satisfied:	It is either daytime (Input A) or an imaging request is active (Input B) and it mustbe currently over the desighated target aréa (Input C). The satellite operator is required to design a logic circuit using only one OR gate and one AND gate and then construct a truth table showing how the circuit will behave under all possible input conditions. However, he finds it as a challenge to do all this to his limited knowledge on logic gate and seeks helps from the students. As a physics student, help your fellow students in responding to their activity.

questions.text: A deadly illness emerged in a refugee camp, affecting many residents. Investigations traced the source to tinned food distributed through an emergency relief program. Tests later confirnmed that the food had been contaminated with Cobalt-60, a radioactive isotope, likely due to exposure during packaging or storage near a facility that handles radioactive materials. A Geiger-Müller (GM) tube was used to measure the raioactive activity in the food over time. The data collected is shown below: Table 1.* To assess potential internal damage, doctors recommended low-dose diagnostic X-ray scans, but the local council opposed the proposal, expressing concerns about possible cancer risks. Hint: The food is considered unsafe if its radiation activity remains above the background level of 90 counts per minute.

questions.text: A dairy company manager notices a sharp drop in sales from one of his vendors. Upon inquiry, he finds that customers have complained the milk is too watery. The vendor denies adding water tothe milk. Since diluted milk has a lower density, the manager seeks your assistance to verify the claim by testing the density of the milk sample. You also learn that the milk is transported in a 120kg aluminium container, with both the milk and container initially at 30°C.The milk must be cooled to a temperature not nore than 4.0°C to prevent spoilage. The container holds 150 litres of milk and is placed in a refrigerated van powered by the vehicle's engine. The refrigerator draws 10,000,000 J per hour from the materials in it but can only work for 45 minutes before its mandatory turned off. Hint: ii. Density of puremilk 1030 kg/m iv. 1 litre = 0.001m3 i SHCof milk = 1040 JkgK1 ii SHC of aluminium = 900 Jkg 'K-1

subTasks.text: Explain to the manager the steps to be followed	to determine the density of milk in order to check whether it was diluted.

subTasks.text: Determine whether the milk will be adequately	cooled?

questions.text: After their match, Buddu FC attributed their victory to the spiked football shoes worn by the players. They also followed their doctor's advice to wear woolen jackets and drink hot water from a vacuum flask and were surprised that the water remained hot despite the cool weather. On their return journey, part of the team traveled in a 2,600 kg Pajero that accelerated uniformlyfrom rest for 1.3 km in 3 mintes before colliding head-on with a 1.8-tonne saloon car moving at 12 m/s in the opposite direction. The vehicles moved for about 4 seconds before coming to rest. Several players were injured upon impact,and the crash generated heat, sound,and sparks, causing panic within the nearby residents. Some claimed the vehicles damaged the pavements of a roundabout 8 meters from the collision point, but the Pajero driver denied this, stating they stopped before reaching it. Hint: 1 tonne = 1000 kg

subTasks.label: a
subTasks.text: Explain	how the use of spiked football shoes contributed to Buddu FC's performance, and why the advice to wear woolen jackets and drink hot water from a vacuum flask was important	after the match.

subTasks.label: b
subTasks.text: Explain how a vacuum flask is able to keep water hot for several hours.

subTasks.label: c
subTasks.text: Explain why passengers hit objects inside the vehicle and suggest measures that can be taken to prevent such incidents	from happening again.

subTasks.label: d
subTasks.text: Based on the given data, assess whether the vehicles	caused the damage to the pavements.

questions.text: A milling factory far from the national power station has consistently over exceeded its monthly electricity budget of UGX 850,000. It relies on diesel-powered AC generators, which consume large amounts of fuel daily, leading to high operational costs. To solve this, the government plans to install high-voltagetransmission lines to deliver AC power from the power station to the factory. A step-uptransformerat the power station raises the voltage to 11,000 V to allow for eficient long-distance transmission. At the receiving end (the factory), a step-down transforner is required to teduce the voltage to 440 V, which is suitable for operating industrial machines. The model of the factory's transformer to be used is shown below.
